name: Eleventh Dream Day
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: Rick Rizzo and Janet Beveridge Bean started the band in a Louisville punk house and took it to Chicago, where Atlantic offered seven records and kept them for three. They've kept making loud ones, on their own schedule, ever since.

eras.title: Out of 1069 Bardstown Road
eras.text: Eleventh Dream Day came out of a Louisville punk house and landed in Chicago. Rizzo's guitar leaned on Neil Young, Bean moved from guitar to the drums, and one night in a Louisville studio put them on the majors' radar.

q: Comedy Minus One's bio on 1069 Bardstown Road
years.src: Comedy Minus One · Wikipedia: Eleventh Dream Day
years.h: Rick Rizzo and Janet Beveridge Bean meet in a Louisville punk house
years.p: Bean was practicing at 1069 Bardstown Road with the Zoo Directors and [[Tara Key|c75b1d24-3127-4dba-88d2-40a263995b1d]] when Rizzo talked her into moving to Chicago. Shu Shubat plays bass.
years.xp: Comedy Minus One, the band's later label, uses "punk rock think tank" for 1069 Bardstown Road. Rizzo and Bean started the band in Chicago and eventually married. Bean began on guitar, then moved to the drums, where she stayed, singing from behind the kit.

years.src: Comedy Minus One · Wikipedia: Eleventh Dream Day
years.h: Doug McCombs and Baird Figi lock in the line-up
years.p: Bassist [[Doug McCombs|2bf77a32-29bb-432f-afe1-bde92b431c23]] replaces Shu Shubat, and guitarist [[Baird Figi|f294e1ac-58bf-4355-925a-8c9875c155f4]] joins Rizzo and Bean. Comedy Minus One's bio sums them up in that line.

years.h: A self-titled EP on Amoeba sets the template
years.p: Eleventh Dream Day is the band's first record. Wikipedia describes the sound as Neil Young-inspired electric guitar workouts mixed with punk energy.

years.h: Half the night goes to a buzz in Rick Rizzo's amp
years.p: Prairie School Freakout is recorded at Artist Recording Service in Louisville between 11 pm and 5 am. Fifteen songs, and the buzz eats half the night.
years.xp: The liner notes tell it: fifteen songs in six hours, half of that spent trying to kill the hum coming out of Rizzo's amplifier. They gave up and made the buzz part of the record. The band co-produced with Louisville guitarist [[Wink O'Bannon|c8e17b50-f4f9-4151-9946-5fad012dce04]], who would join five years later.

years.src: Wikipedia: Prairie School Freakout · Wikipedia: Eleventh Dream Day
years.h: Prairie School Freakout gets the majors calling
years.p: Out on Amoeba, the band's first album later makes Spin's list of 80 excellent records of the 1980s.
years.xp: Critics lined up behind it. Greg Kot called it both steeped in tradition and ahead of its time. Jim DeRogatis called it the band's masterpiece, and AllMusic said Eleventh Dream Day never rocked harder. Thrill Jockey reissued it in 2003 with the Wayne EP and the band's music videos.

eras.title: Seven records promised
eras.text: Atlantic signed the band to seven records and got three, plus two modern rock chart singles and a line-up change. Then the label let them go, and the band made its favorite record for an indie.

years.h: Atlantic offers seven records
years.p: After the EP and Prairie School Freakout, Atlantic Records chases the band and puts a seven-record contract on the table, according to Comedy Minus One's bio.

years.h: Beet goes down in four days for Atlantic
years.p: Producer Gary Waleik oversees the June 1989 sessions. The Chicago Reader called the record a hoot; Robert Christgau gave it a C+.

years.src: Wikipedia: Eleventh Dream Day · Wikipedia: Beet (album)
yt: Full show at Peabody's Down Under, Cleveland, Feb 1, 1990
years.h: Testify climbs to No. 26 on the modern rock chart
years.p: The single from Beet peaks at No. 26 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart. Atlantic also presses Borscht, a promo-only release.

years.cap: Flyer for a Derby Eve show in Louisville with Sun Agilwet and Firehose, Friday May 3, c. 1991
years.h: Lived to Tell puts Rose of Jericho at No. 27
years.p: The second Atlantic album produces a second chart single, one place below Testify.

years.h: Baird Figi leaves, and a co-producer takes his place
years.p: Matthew "Wink" O'Bannon, who co-produced Prairie School Freakout in Louisville, becomes the band's second guitarist.

years.h: El Moodio gets made twice
years.p: The band starts it in Chicago with [[Brad Wood|58c8c056-4f9a-4a3b-8dd9-69b06bb23c28]], then remakes it at Sorcerer Sound in New York with producer Jim Rondinelli for Atlantic.
years.xp: Rizzo and Bean wrote nine of the ten songs; O'Bannon brought Murder. [[Velvet Crush|dadd10f1-9db4-4a35-b939-9469029deab5]]'s Ric Menck drums on That's the Point. The shelved Chicago sessions with Wood at Idful finally came out in 2013 as New Moodio.

years.src: Wikipedia: El Moodio · Wikipedia: Eleventh Dream Day · Comedy Minus One
years.h: Atlantic drops the band after three of seven albums
years.p: El Moodio was the shot at a commercial record. It didn't sell.
years.xp: Reviews split. Rolling Stone said the band had passion to burn; the Washington Post said the album never pulled together its Velvet Underground, Neil Young and Dream Syndicate influences. The band toured North America behind it anyway, then walked back into Chicago's indie world.

yt: Full show in Cologne, Aug 19, 1994, with Ira Kaplan of Yo La Tengo
years.h: Ursa Major opens with History of Brokeback
years.p: [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] records it at Idful in Chicago and Brad Wood mixes it for Atavistic. The instrumental's title later becomes the name of Doug McCombs's own band, [[Brokeback|e3fa3b7a-b883-4432-9152-ed0cf4d5c19c]].
years.xp: Planned as an EP, it grew into an album and became what the band calls its collective favorite. [[Bundy K. Brown|940101f1-79c7-40ac-98d3-7b924b244a8e]] and McEntire, both in the orbit of [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]], added parts. The Chicago Tribune ranked it the ninth best album of 1994.

years.h: Wink O'Bannon leaves, and the band goes part-time
years.p: Rizzo goes back to college for an education degree, Bean puts her time into [[Freakwater|50e68a47-b6e4-4178-84d5-8955206a0b7f]], and McCombs into [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]].

eras.title: Part-timers on Thrill Jockey
eras.text: The band never broke up; it just stopped being a job. Thrill Jockey, home to Tortoise and Freakwater, became home base, and records arrived whenever the members' other bands allowed.

years.h: Three years on, Eighth arrives on Thrill Jockey
years.p: The first record for the label comes with Rizzo, Bean and McCombs still at the core.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the Thrill Jockey albums as balancing Neil Young-influenced guitar with ambient soundscaping.

years.h: Mark Greenberg of the Coctails joins on keyboards
years.p: [[Mark Greenberg|67e0ccc5-9dc9-4f23-b037-e94a53520563]] of [[The Coctails|0b94e13b-4ee7-448c-be31-5d125d8717ef]] plays on Stalled Parade, the band's second Thrill Jockey album.

years.cap: Rick Rizzo, with Mark Greenberg behind him, on stage
years.h: Prairie School Freakout comes back, with a Neil Young cover
years.p: Thrill Jockey reissues the 1988 album with the Wayne EP, the band's videos and bonus tracks, including a version of Young's Southern Pacific.

years.cap: Rick Rizzo and Doug McCombs at the Empty Bottle, Chicago, May 19, 2006
years.h: Six years after Stalled Parade, Zeroes and Ones
years.p: The band's third Thrill Jockey album comes out April 25.

eras.title: The Hideout years
eras.text: Chicago's Hideout became a workshop, a long residency where new songs got loud in front of people before anyone recorded them. A second guitarist came back for the first time since 1994.

years.cap: Eleventh Dream Day at Lincoln Hall, Chicago, April 22, 2011
years.h: Riot Now! is out March 15
years.p: The fourth Thrill Jockey album. The band plays Lincoln Hall in Chicago that April.

years.h: James Elkington brings the second guitar back
years.p: [[James Elkington|0b4020a0-0126-4574-bbed-d9109ed60b8a]] of [[Brokeback|e3fa3b7a-b883-4432-9152-ed0cf4d5c19c]] joins. Thrill Jockey says it's the first time since 1994 the band has recorded with a second guitarist.

years.h: New Moodio, the El Moodio Atlantic never put out
years.p: Comedy Minus One releases the Chicago sessions the band cut with Brad Wood at Idful.

years.cap: Rizzo, Bean, McCombs, Greenberg and Elkington, c. 2015
yt: Satellite, live at the Hideout, Apr 27, 2014
years.h: Works for Tomorrow gets built onstage at the Hideout
years.p: The band works the songs up in a long residency at Chicago's Hideout, then Greenberg records it at the Loft, [[Wilco|9e53f84d-ef44-4c16-9677-5fd4d78cbd7d]]'s studio, and Mayfair Recordings.
years.xp:
Ten tracks, 43 minutes. Thrill Jockey pitched the five-piece record as a band still moving forward, and singled out Bean's singing, which it described as having an "animalistic urgency."

Martin Wenk of Calexico and Rich Parenti play horns. Critics liked it.

years.cap: Jim Elkington, Rick Rizzo, Doug McCombs, Mark Greenberg and Janet Beveridge Bean, 2021
years.h: No warning, then a double album
years.p: Since Grazed lands on Comedy Minus One on April 2, 2021. The label calls the band semi-retired, but still making records.
